mechanism_relevant_findings: Phosphate glasses exhibit high proton mobility arising from the strong hydrogen bonding of OH groups.
The use of electrochemical alkali-proton substitution (APS) results in increased proton conductivity.

numerical_findings.conditions: for glasses prepared by low temperature melting

arrhenius_vtf_findings: The glass demonstrated stability for a long time at temperatures up to 280 °C indicating potential for Arrhenius behavior.
limitations: Most previous studies focused on increasing the concentration of proton carriers, while dehydration occurs at temperatures higher than 230 °C.

relevance_judgement.reason: The findings support the development of intermediate temperature fuel cells utilizing phosphate glasses.
